findings.title: ensureSymlink 'differs and must replace' branch has no test
findings.detail: ensureSymlink has three branches: (1) dst is already the correct symlink → no-op; (2) dst exists as a symlink to a different target → remove and re-link; (3) dst exists as a regular file → error. The manager_test.go and rollback_test.go exercise branch (1) incidentally, and branch (3) is never exercised at all. Branch (2) — the 'moved profile source is picked up without manual intervention' case — is critical for the rename workflow but has no dedicated test. TestRenameUpdatesSymlinksToPointAtNewSource in manager_test.go calls Rename which calls RemoveSymlinks then BuildSymlinks, so it never hits ensureSymlink with a pre-existing stale link; it hits the 'no dst' path.

findings.title: ensureSymlink 'regular file exists at dst' branch never tested
findings.detail: The else branch at line 119 returns an error when dst is a regular file (not a symlink). No test creates a regular file at a SharedItem path inside ConfigDir and then calls BuildSymlinks or RefreshSymlinks. This is a meaningful defensive error path: it fires when the user or Claude has written a real file where ccp expects to own a symlink.

findings.title: copyTree symlink branch is never exercised
findings.detail: copyTree has three cases: directory, symlink, and regular file. TestCreateFromProfileClonesSource in manager_test.go seeds only regular files (settings.json) and calls copyTree indirectly via Create with FromProfile. The symlink branch (lines 88-94) is never hit. If the source profile contains a symlink, copyTree will reproduce it — this is intentional — but no test verifies the reproduced symlink points to the right target or that permission errors on os.Readlink are surfaced.

findings.title: sync pull with actual remote conflict (diverged commits) is not tested
findings.detail: TestPullRefusesDirtyWorkingTreeWithoutForce tests the 'uncommitted local changes' guard. TestCrossMachineCloneRoundTrip tests a clean push-then-clone flow. Neither test exercises the scenario where machine A and machine B have each made independent commits and then B attempts Pull — i.e., a genuine divergence that git would resolve via merge or surface as a non-fast-forward conflict. The Pull function delegates to go-git's w.Pull(), which returns an error on a true conflict; this error path is never exercised. This is the case users will hit in practice when two machines edit profiles concurrently.

findings.title: sync pull --force path (backup-then-hard-reset) is not tested end-to-end
findings.detail: Pull's force branch (lines 287-297) calls backupProfilesDir then hardReset before pulling. No test covers this path: there is no test that sets Force=true and verifies (a) profiles/ is backed up, (b) the reset discards local changes, and (c) the subsequent pull succeeds. The sync_pull.go CLI wrapper has no tests at all for the --force flag codepath.

findings.title: mergeCopyDir in sync.go (CloneOrOpen clone path) has no dedicated test
findings.detail: mergeCopyDir is only exercised indirectly via TestCrossMachineCloneRoundTrip → CloneOrOpen. The test verifies that a profile file lands with correct content, but does not exercise: (1) the symlink branch inside mergeCopyDir (lines 478-485), (2) what happens when dst already has a file that differs from src (overwrite semantics), or (3) the edge case where src is empty (profiles/ not yet present in the remote). The symlink branch inside mergeCopyDir is especially risky because filepath.Walk does not follow symlinks by default, so the ModeSymlink check on info.Mode() will never fire for a symlinked entry traversed by Walk — the branch is dead code.

findings.title: CLI sync commands (pull, push, setup, status) have zero test coverage
findings.detail: sync_pull.go, sync_push.go, sync_setup.go, and sync_status.go contain CLI glue logic that is distinct from the sync package unit tests. The CLI layer handles: (1) the 'not a sync repo' guard, (2) the --force backup + prune sequence, (3) the --dry-run switch-case logic in push (committed vs not-committed × dry-run × no-remote produces four distinct code paths), and (4) the fallback() display helper in status. None of these paths are exercised by any test. The switch-case in sync_push.go lines 30-43 (four cases) has zero coverage.

findings.title: resolveShellrc fallback priority not tested
findings.detail: resolveShellrc has four branches: (1) explicit path with ~ expansion, (2) explicit path without ~, (3) iterating candidates until one exists (.zshrc, .bashrc, .bash_profile), (4) fallback to ~/.zshrc when none exist. TestCreateWithAliasWritesBlock in profile_cmd_test.go reaches branch 4 (no shellrc present → creates .zshrc) but never tests branch 3 (a .bashrc exists but no .zshrc → should pick .bashrc). The ~ expansion in branch 1 is also untested. These are meaningful behavioral differences for users on bash-primary systems.

findings.title: profile_refresh.go 'no-name refreshes all profiles' branch has no test
findings.detail: newProfileRefreshCmd handles two cases: a named profile (len(args)==1) and all profiles (len(args)==0 → List then refresh each). No test in the test suite calls 'ccp profile refresh' — neither the named nor the all-profiles variant. The all-profiles branch, in particular, exercises a loop that short-circuits on the first error; this error propagation is unverified.

findings.title: profile_rename.go manifest update (active profile tracking) has no targeted test
findings.detail: The rename command has a branch that updates the manifest's ActiveProfile when the renamed profile was the active one (lines 35-40). TestProfileLifecycle in profile_cmd_test.go does test rename after activate, and it verifies `ccp current` returns the new name — so this path IS exercised. However, the inverse — renaming a non-active profile when another profile is active — is not tested to confirm the active profile field is left unchanged.

findings.title: profile_show.go 'absent profile' and 'no active profile' branches untested
findings.detail: newProfileShowCmd has two distinct error paths: (1) no args and no active profile set → returns 'no profile specified' error; (2) named profile that doesn't exist → returns 'profile not found' error. TestProfileLifecycle exercises the happy path for 'show' but neither error branch is tested. The 'absent' profile case reaches profile.New then !pr.Exists() which is straightforward but the countEntries helper called for directory items (line 46-50) is never driven with a directory that has items (only present/absent is tested via the lifecycle test).

findings.title: exec.go 'nonzero child exit code' branch not tested
findings.detail: TestExecSetsClaudeConfigDirForChildProcess in m3_test.go tests the happy path (child exits 0). The exec.go RunE has a branch at lines 60-62 that casts err to *exec.ExitError and calls os.Exit with the child's exit code. This branch is never tested. Because it calls os.Exit directly (not returning an error), it would also bypass deferred cleanup in cobra. A test running '/bin/sh -c "exit 42"' would verify the propagation behavior and catch any regression where the ExitError cast fails.

findings.title: Rollback with a partial backup (only source, no runtime dir) is not tested
findings.detail: TestRollbackRestoresDeletedProfile exercises the full backup (profiles-work + claude-work). TestRollbackRefusesIfNameClashes tests the name-collision guard. No test exercises a backup that contains only a 'profiles-<name>' entry with no 'claude-<name>' — which happens when the profile was created but never used (ConfigDir was never created). In this case the moves slice contains only one move instead of two; the code handles this correctly, but it is not verified.

findings.title: Fish shell snippet is never executed to verify correctness
findings.detail: TestShellInitPosixActuallyRunsInSh sources the POSIX snippet in /bin/sh and verifies CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set correctly. There is an equivalent test for the fish snippet's content string (TestShellInitFishContainsSetGX) but it only does a string search — it never executes the fish snippet in an actual fish shell to verify quoting, the awk invocation, or the set -gx semantics. Fish shell is available in most CI macOS images. The fish snippet uses a distinct variable-scoping model (set -l vs local) where quoting bugs produce no error but wrong behavior.

findings.title: npm/install.js tar extractor has no tests at all
findings.detail: The npm/ directory contains a hand-rolled USTAR tar extractor (extractBinary) with no test file. There is no package.json 'test' script and no test runner configured. The extractor handles redirects, block rounding (Math.ceil(size/512)*512), type-code filtering ('0' for regular files), and a basename match. Goreleaser may emit subdirectory paths (e.g. 'ccp_0.1.0_darwin_arm64/ccp'), and path.basename() makes this work — but there is no test that verifies a real or synthetic tar buffer is extracted correctly. A malformed size field (non-octal chars, truncated buffer) causes parseInt to return NaN → size=0 → infinite loop at offset = dataStart. This is a silent install failure path.

findings.title: SIGKILL mid-operation atomicity is not tested
findings.detail: Create uses an os.Mkdir guard and a defer-based rollback (lines 51-57) to ensure partial state is cleaned up on failure. Delete uses os.Rename to move source then runtime into backup — rename is atomic on POSIX. However, no test verifies what state the filesystem is in if the process is killed between the source rename and the runtime rename in Delete (lines 126-137 of manager.go), or between os.Mkdir and BuildSymlinks in Create. In practice the defer cleanup in Create handles in-process failures but not SIGKILL. The plan called for testing SIGKILL-mid-switch; this is entirely absent. Confidence is moderate because SIGKILL simulation requires process spawning, which is harder to write but not impossible with exec.Cmd + Process.Kill.

findings.title: Backup Prune with keep=0 (no-op guard) is tested only implicitly
findings.detail: Prune has an early return when keep <= 0 (line 36-38). No test calls Prune(base, 0) to verify the no-op guard. TestPruneKeepsNewest always passes keep=2. This is a low-value gap but means a caller who accidentally passes 0 (expecting 'prune all') would silently not prune.

findings.title: Doctor 'runtime path is not a directory' branch untested
findings.detail: checkRuntime has a branch at lines 72-78 that fires when the ConfigDir path exists but is a regular file rather than a directory. TestDoctorMissingRuntimeDirIsWarning removes the dir. No test creates a regular file at pr.ConfigDir to trigger the 'is not a directory' error finding.

findings.title: Doctor 'missing runtime symlink for SharedItem present in source' branch untested
findings.detail: Pass 1 of checkRuntime reports an error when a SharedItem exists in SourceDir but has no corresponding symlink in ConfigDir. No test seeds a source file and then removes the corresponding symlink (without removing the source) to trigger this finding. TestDoctorDetectsDanglingSymlink removes the source after creating the symlink, which exercises Pass 2, not Pass 1.

findings.title: CI matrix covers only latest OS versions, not exact Go version range
findings.detail: The CI matrix runs ubuntu-latest and macos-latest with the Go version pinned by go.mod. No matrix dimension exercises an older minor Go version (e.g. the go.mod minimum). The fslock package uses unix.Flock from golang.org/x/sys which is stable, but the go-git dependency has had breaking changes across minor versions. Confidence is moderate because the actual minimum Go version from go.mod is not visible in the reviewed files; the risk is real but depends on what minimum is declared.

residual_risks.description: The sync pull conflict path (diverged commits between two machines) calls go-git's w.Pull which internally attempts a merge. If go-git returns a merge conflict error, the Pull function returns it unwrapped. There is no test verifying the error message is actionable or that the filesystem is in a consistent state after a failed merge attempt.

mergeCopyDir's symlink branch (sync.go line 478-485) uses filepath.Walk, which does not call the walk function for symlinks — it stat-follows them. This means the ModeSymlink check will never be true for entries encountered during a Walk traversal; the branch is unreachable dead code. If the cloned tree contains symlinks, they will be walked as their targets (file or dir), not reproduced as symlinks. No test catches this.

npm/install.js extractBinary: if parseInt(octalString, 8) returns NaN (malformed tar size field), size becomes 0. Then offset = dataStart + Math.ceil(0/512)*512 = dataStart + 0 = dataStart = offset+512. Next iteration: same header, infinite loop. CI never runs install.js, and there are no tests for the extractor.

profile.Delete performs two sequential os.Rename calls (source then runtime). Between these two calls, if the process exits abnormally, the source is in the backup but the runtime dir remains in place. On next run, profile.New(p, name).Exists() returns false (source gone) but the runtime dir still exists. Future Create with the same name will call BuildSymlinks and potentially collide with stale runtime content. No test or documentation covers this partial-delete recovery path.

sshAuthFromEnv in sync/auth.go is entirely untested. The SSH agent path, the key-file fallback path, and the 'neither available' path (returns nil) all have zero coverage. Passing nil Auth to go-git Push/Pull causes authentication failures for SSH remotes that are not caught in CI because the cross-machine test uses a local bare repo (file://) that requires no auth.

testing_gaps.question: Are the file-system mutation paths (delete, rename, rollback, force-pull) tested for partial failures, concurrent operations, permission errors, corrupted inputs?
testing_gaps.answer: Partially. Delete, Rename, and Rollback happy paths are tested. Concurrent operation safety is tested only for the fslock (mutual exclusion). Partial failure mid-Delete (SIGKILL between two Rename calls) is not tested. Permission errors are not tested anywhere. force-pull (backup + hard-reset + pull) has no test at all.

testing_gaps.question: Are SIGKILL-mid-operation failure modes tested?
testing_gaps.answer: No. The plan called for this but there are no tests that spawn a subprocess, kill it mid-operation, and verify filesystem consistency. The defer-based rollback in Create is exercised by in-process panics/errors but not by external kill signals.

testing_gaps.question: Is the tar extractor in npm/install.js exercised at all?
testing_gaps.answer: No. There are no tests whatsoever for npm/install.js. The extractBinary function, the redirect-following HTTP logic, and the platform detection map all have zero test coverage. There is no test script in npm/package.json.

testing_gaps.question: Is `ccp sync pull` tested with an actual conflict between local and remote commits?
testing_gaps.answer: No. sync_test.go tests the dirty-working-tree guard and the clean clone round-trip. A scenario where both sides have independent commits and Pull fails with a non-fast-forward or merge conflict error is not tested.

testing_gaps.question: Are the fish shell snippets verified to parse?
testing_gaps.answer: No. TestShellInitFishContainsSetGX checks for the 'set -gx CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR' string but does not execute the snippet in fish. There is no equivalent of TestShellInitPosixActuallyRunsInSh for fish.

testing_gaps.question: Does the CI matrix exercise Linux + macOS adequately?
testing_gaps.answer: Adequately for basic correctness: ubuntu-latest and macos-latest are both in the matrix with -race enabled. Gaps: no Windows (not in scope given flock), no older Go minor version testing, and the release job only runs on ubuntu-latest so goreleaser cross-compilation is not validated on macOS.
